answer: Persistent routing relic: each agent identity must anchor a forwarding path through a small set of relay neighbors, recorded as a signed route history. A valid pulse requires the identity's traffic to traverse at least three distinct relays per epoch, each confirming timing and hop count. Relays near a registration knoll (dense cluster of fresh peers) are weighted lower, so fake neighborhoods yield weak signals. Enforcement: identities below the relay-diversity threshold lose routing priority and quoting rights.
